card.name: Schedule changes: daily vs workweek frequency
card.fires_on: Small words and word parts right before a frequency or schedule phrase, such as 'twice daily', 'once daily', or 'six-day week'. Seen in dosing-interval text and in talk of workweek length.

modes.label: Dosing frequency
modes.description: Linking word or word part just before 'once daily', 'twice daily' or 'dosing interval' in dose instructions.
modes.example: In such patients an increase in dosage<< or>> twice daily administration may be warranted.

modes.label: Workweek length
modes.description: Word in a passage about the length of the working week, before a day-count such as six-day or forty hours.
modes.example: Stalin demands “the end of the five-day week and a return<< to>> the six-day week.”

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about channels or counts per period, which fits a schedule or frequency that comes next.
card.plain: It lights up just before a phrase saying how often something is done, like twice daily or a six-day week.
